draft.title: Compulsory voting
card: In Australia, voting in federal and state elections is compulsory for enrolled voters. Voters must have their name marked off the roll, and a person who does not vote without a valid reason may be sent a notice and asked to explain.
Compulsory voting brings high turnout. Turnout is the share of enrolled voters who vote. In Australia it is usually about 90% or more.
Governments are chosen by almost all voters, so the result reflects the views of the whole community, not only the most motivated people.
Some people argue that citizens should be free to choose not to vote, because they see voting as a right and not a duty.
draft.remember: Compulsory voting brings high turnout, but some argue voters should be free to choose.

a.q: Which of these is an argument against compulsory voting?
opts: People should be free to choose not to vote
Governments should be chosen by most voters
Turnout at elections would be much lower
Most enrolled voters would be marked off the roll
a.why: The argument against rests on freedom of choice: voting is seen as a right, so people should be able to decline. The option about governments chosen by most voters is an argument for compulsory voting.
a.clue: Look for the option about freedom, not turnout.

b.q: In a federal election, 92% of enrolled voters in Jaya's town vote. Her friend Ben says this shows most people there love politics. What is the best reply?
opts: High turnout is expected because voting is compulsory
High turnout shows people there are very well informed
Turnout is high because the town has few enrolled voters
Turnout is high because people there pay more tax
b.why: Compulsory voting brings high turnout, so a high figure does not show that people love politics. The tempting option about being well informed treats turnout as a sign of knowledge, which the card does not support.
b.clue: What does Australia require of enrolled voters?

a.best: People should be free to choose not to vote

b.best: High turnout is expected because voting is compulsory

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for the option about freedom, not turnout' names the key word of the right option, which is the only option about freedom. A student can pick it without knowing the idea.

a.q: Which of these is an argument against compulsory voting?
opts: People should be free to choose not to vote
Governments should be chosen by most voters
Voting is a duty that every citizen owes
Results should reflect the whole community
a.why: The argument against rests on freedom of choice: voting is seen as a right, so people should be able to decline. Seeing voting as a duty, or wanting governments chosen by most voters, supports compulsory voting.
